content: 1. Cenobamate reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. This interaction necessitates close monitoring and potential therapy modification. Women using oral contraceptives concurrently with cenobamate should be advised to use additional or alternative non-hormonal birth control methods. 2. Cephalexin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Ceritinib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Chloramphenicol decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 5. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Ciprofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 7. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 8. Clindamycin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 9. Clobazam decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and etonogestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Clobazam is a weak CYP3A4 inducer, and its concurrent use may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives. Additional non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 10. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of clonazepam by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ethinylestradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, leading to increased serum concentrations of co-administered benzodiazepines. 11. Conivaptan increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Cyclosporine increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ethinylestradiol also increases cyclosporine levels through an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 14. Darifenacin increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Danicopan increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol through mechanisms involving BCRP substrates. Dose reduction of BCRP substrates may be necessary. Caution and monitoring are advised. 16. Darunavir has a dual effect on ethinylestradiol and etonogestrel, either increasing or decreasing their levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 17. Dasatinib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 18. Deferasirox decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and etonogestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 19. DHEA (herbal) increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Demeclocycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 21. Diazepam levels are increased by ethinylestradiol due to decreased metabolism. Ethinylestradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, leading to increased serum concentrations. Caution and monitoring are advised. 22. Dicloxacillin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 23. Doxycycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 24. Dronedarone increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 26. Elafibranor decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods or barrier methods should be used during elafibranor treatment and for at least three weeks after the last dose. 27. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. 28. Eltrombopag levels are increased by ethinylestradiol due to inhibition of CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases the levels of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Cobicistat is a CYP3A4 inhibitor and contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates associated with serious or life-threatening events. 30. Encorafenib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 31. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate) decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Antibiotics may decrease hormonal contraceptive efficacy. 32. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and etonogestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 33. Exenatide (injectable solution/suspension) may reduce the efficacy of oral contraceptives by slowing gastric emptying, which decreases the extent and rate of oral medication absorption. Patients should take oral contraceptives at least one hour before exenatide administration. Estrogens may also impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients. 34. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. Caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 36. Flibanserin levels are increased by ethinylestradiol due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Adverse effects of flibanserin may increase when co-administered with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are advised. 37. Fluvoxamine levels are increased by ethinylestradiol due to inhibition of CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 38. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 39. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 40. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 41. Fostemsavir increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Avoid co-administration or modify the dose of BCRP substrates when used with fostemsavir. Ethinylestradiol doses should not exceed 30 mcg/day. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 42. Gemifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 43. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 44. Green tea levels are increased by ethinylestradiol due to decreased elimination. Caution and monitoring are advised. 45. Griseofulvin decreases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 46. Hemin effects are decreased by ethinylestradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Drugs that increase delta-aminolevulinic acid synthetase may reduce hemin efficacy. Caution and monitoring are advised. 47. Hyaluronidase effects are decreased by estrogens, which may render tissues partially resistant to hyaluronidase action. Larger amounts of hyaluronidase may be required for equivalent dispersing effects. Caution and monitoring are advised. 48. Hydrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 49. Iloperidone increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may lead to increased plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 50. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 51. Insulin (aspart, degludec, detemir) effects are decreased by ethinylestradiol and etonogestrel through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients.
